TPP Likely To Force Canada To Repeal Local Data Protection Laws

Could someone describe to me what the negative and positive effects for corporations, the Canadian government, and Canadian people that this would have? I'm not sure what the potential impact of repealing these laws would be

Not forcing organizations to store sensitive data locally usually means it's going to be stored "in the cloud", and most cloud storage providers are in the states. Once there, it's under American Government jurisdiction (aka NSA). I don't think anyone wants their medical records to be available to unrelated 3rd parties.

Of course I'd argue that no one should store any data in places under American jurisdiction, but that's more of a personal opinion.

Semi related: I work for the federal government and they are outsourcing all email to Bell. I can't say I trust them with handling it properly. I often (indirectly) deal with them for other services and every time something happens, they just shrug and say nothing can be done. If it's inside the organization then at least there's always some superior that you can go to and complain.

Edit: went on a bit of a rant, but what you want to get out of this is that when it's not under your local jurisdiction, you have no say over how the data is handled. If you live in BC and your data is in BC, you vote on what protections your data gets. This is not the case with it being elsewhere. For personal things it doesn't matter as much because everyone can make the decision themselves, but an organization stores all of its data in one place, so everyone is affected.
